$comment: Generated by orchestrator/backend/scripts/generate_agent_schemas.py from app.api.code_analysis.AnalysisResultRecord plus agent-side overlays where the CLI contract is intentionally stricter than the backend model.

queue_item_id.title: Queue Item Id
queue_item_id.description: ID of the claimed code_analysis_queue item this result corresponds to. The backend derives file_id from this queue item.

file_id.title: File Id
file_id.description: Optional consistency check. When supplied, it must match the file_id on queue_item_id; the backend records the queue-derived file_id.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Name of the agent that produced this result.

hypothesis.title: Hypothesis
hypothesis.description: The vulnerability hypothesis tested. What could go wrong and why.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Evidence supporting the disposition. For findings: code snippet + taint path + guard failure. For clean: brief reasoning why no vulnerability exists.

evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref
evidence_ref.description: Optional engagement-owned artifact path supporting the disposition. A finding or suspicious closeout requires non-empty inline evidence or this artifact reference on a current result for the active lease.

disposition.title: Disposition
disposition.description: Analysis result. finding: confirmed vulnerability. suspicious: needs variant analysis or deeper context. clean: no vulnerability. needs_context: blocked on missing code.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: high: full taint trace + guards evaluated. medium: trace but unresolved callees. low: pattern match only.

finding_slug.title: Finding Slug
finding_slug.description: If disposition is 'finding', the slug of the assessment_findings record created. Empty otherwise.

cwe_id.title: Cwe Id
cwe_id.description: Specific CWE ID (for example, CWE-122, CWE-190). Must be specific, not generic (CWE-119).

slot_type.title: Slot Type
slot_type.description: Shannon slot type classification of the vulnerability (for example, BUFFER-WRITE, FORMAT-STRING, INTEGER-OVERFLOW, USE-AFTER-FREE, CMD-INJECTION).

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Additional notes, context expansion requests, or follow-up recommendations.

audit_metadata.title: Audit Metadata
audit_metadata.description: Arbitrary key/value bag for agent-specific audit context (token counts, tool versions, analysis timestamps). Not used for security decisions; included verbatim in audit logs.

family.description: Vulnerability class name (for example, sql-injection, path-traversal)

effort.description: How thoroughly this class was analyzed. 0-20: glanced at imports/exports. 20-40: checked obvious sinks. 40-60: examined entry-point functions with basic taint tracing. 60-80: full taint tracing on entry-point chains + error paths. 80-100: exhaustive analysis including cross-file flows and bypass attempts.

disposition.description: Whether this class was analyzed or marked not-applicable for this file. Use not_applicable when the class cannot apply (e.g., buffer-overflow in a pure Python module).

not_applicable.description: Shorthand flag: true means disposition=not_applicable. Backend accepts either form.

functions_analyzed.description: Number of functions in this file examined for this vulnerability class

entry_chains_traced.description: Number of entry-point chains from call graph traced end-to-end for this class

total_entry_chains.description: Total entry-point chains relevant to this class (denominator for coverage ratio)

notes.description: Brief explanation of what was or was not analyzed and why

cwe_coverage.title: Cwe Coverage
cwe_coverage.description: Per-vulnerability-class effort records. Effort is a gradient (0-100), not binary.

file_path.description: Repo-relative path to the file that should be re-analyzed (e.g., 'src/url_helpers.c').

reason.description: Why this file needs re-analysis — name the specific function/callee and the data flow that crosses the boundary.

vuln_class.description: Vulnerability class to focus on in the downstream file (matches cwe_coverage family names, e.g., 'buffer-overflow').

cross_file_triggers.title: Cross File Triggers
cross_file_triggers.description: Files reachable via call graph whose analysis should be (re)triggered based on findings in this file. Only emit when a taint flow actually crosses the file boundary.

title: Code Analysis Result
description: Per-function analysis result payload recorded by code-vuln-hunter after analyzing a source code file.

examples.hypothesis: Attacker-controlled URL scheme length passed to memcpy without bounds check
examples.evidence: In parseurl() at line 342, schemelen is derived from user-supplied URL without validation. memcpy(buf, scheme, schemelen) copies attacker-controlled bytes into fixed-size heap buffer.
examples.notes: Guard at line 305 uses signed int comparison allowing negative bypass.

cwe_coverage.notes: Full taint tracing on all memcpy/memmove sinks reachable from network input.
Checked obvious arithmetic on lengths; deeper cross-file flows not yet traced.

cross_file_triggers.reason: parseurl delegates scheme validation to url_validate_scheme() which may have its own bounds issue
